steps.name: Cheery Woman
steps.text: Thank you so much, Silence! I wouldn't have been able to get into Rhine Lab to observe, if not for you.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: No need to thank me. Just doing my job.

steps.name: Cheery Woman
steps.text: It was worth it, waking you up every morning during exam weeks!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I got myself up too.

steps.name: Cheery Woman
steps.text: Twice, in all those years!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Hehe...

steps.name: Cheery Woman
steps.text: There are some real lookers at that company. Tell me the truth—anybody caught your eye?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Huh? Er, no... I've only been here a few days...

steps.name: Cheery Woman
steps.text: Alright, I'll stop teasing you.

steps.name: Cheery Woman
steps.text: I know how obsessed you are with science. You'll never take the initiative to ask anybody out.

steps.name: Cheery Woman
steps.text: To be honest, though, we're a little concerned.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: About what?

steps.name: Cheery Woman
steps.text: Your shyness is your only flaw. Setting aside romance for a moment, we're worried that you won't be able to find a friend to talk to at work.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Y-You don't need to worry.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: All my colleagues are very nice. Nothing to worry about, at all.

steps.name: Cheery Woman
steps.text: ...I guess so.

steps.name: Cheery Woman
steps.text: I'm in Trimounts for three days, which means I'll be around for the weekend.

steps.name: Cheery Woman
steps.text: Let's play all over Trimounts tomorrow!

steps.name: Researcher A
steps.text: Good morning, Silence.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Good morning, Mr. Miller.

steps.name: Researcher B
steps.text: Happy Monday, Chris!

steps.name: Researcher A
steps.text: Happy Monday, Susanna.

steps.name: Researcher B
steps.text: Go anywhere over the weekend?

steps.name: Researcher A
steps.text: Nope. Stayed home and binged a whole season of Blood and Dividends.

steps.name: Researcher B
steps.text: Oh, same here. Stayed up all night to finish it!

steps.name: Researcher A
steps.text: You like that show, Silence?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I... I haven't—

steps.name: Researcher B
steps.text: Let's change the subject... what did you do over the weekend, Silence? Did you go out?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Yes! An old classmate came to Trimounts, and we went to a bunch of places.

steps.name: Researcher B
steps.text: I liked to go out on weekends when I first got here too. There are some choice places in town, which is your favorite?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Trimounts Common.

steps.name: Researcher A
steps.text: The Common? But it's just a bunch of trees. Why would you—

steps.name: Researcher B
steps.text: Chris.

steps.name: Researcher A
steps.text: Oh.

steps.name: Researcher B
steps.text: Well, we've got a thing, better get going. Happy Monday!

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: That's all for this week's agenda. Dismissed.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Silence, a moment of your time.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Of course, Doctor.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: How are things going on the job?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I like the atmosphere here at the company. Everyone is very passionate.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: As you are yourself. Your talent stands out, even in this place. I have high hopes for you.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Thank you...

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: But you have a tendency to be aloof, outside of work.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: There are a lot of young people here. We need to maintain a collegial atmosphere, whether it's having a chat or going out together, some social interaction can be conducive to our work.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Of course you do. Everybody does.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: But the trick is to actually do it.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Anyway, I'm not here to lecture you. I have a task for you.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: I'm not going to force you into a project or a team. Take a look around and see if there's a place in the Structural Section that interests you.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: I'll take your preferences and our needs into account.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Team Sherman... focusing on Originium particle pathology. They're currently working on...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I guess Team 7 fits my preferences better.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But that team is full of veteran researchers... I don't know if it's appropriate to ask to join them...

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: Hey, you over there! Did you see a Liberi woman who looks half-asleep come through here?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Liberi woman... half-asleep?

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: Not you, of course. She has white hair, and she's wearing—

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: Ack, never mind. Doesn't look like she came this way.

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: Don't think she's here, Karen. Let's look somewhere else.

steps.name: Researcher D
steps.text: Where could she have gone? Why can't she just stay put in her room?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: (Are they looking for somebody?)

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: (Liberi woman who looks half-asleep... they might have mistaken me for her, if she didn't have white hair.)

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Only one team left. Let's see... Device #9.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Their office should be here.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: There's a thick coat of dust on the do—

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Liberi woman... white hair... half-asleep...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Are you the patient they're looking for?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Or did you just happen to be unlucky enough to resemble the one they're looking for?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Or are you a member of this team?

steps.name: Team Member
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I see.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I'm Olivia Silence. I just joined Rhine Lab recently. Nice to meet you. What's your name?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Er...
Silence takes a look at the dusty bulletin board. There is only one name on it—Joyce Moore.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Are you Joyce Moore?

steps.name: Joyce Moore
steps.text: Affirmative.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Affirmative?

steps.name: Researcher D
steps.text: Found her—

steps.name: Researcher D
steps.text: You were just over there! Were you lying? Were you trying to help her avoid us?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: No, I didn't—

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: Enough.

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: This is Rhine Lab, not your college dorm! Did you think it was funny, helping her play hide-and-seek?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I'm not...

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: Enough. I don't know what you were thinking, but you're interfering with our work.

steps.name: Researcher D
steps.text: I'll report this!

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Thanks for the explanation. I'll clear this up.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Did something happen to Ms. Moore's team? Why is her name the only one there?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: The team was disbanded after a failed experiment. That office has been empty ever since.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: The names of the others have been removed from the board, but Moore remains hospitalized, so her name has yet to be removed.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: When will she be able to return to work?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Hard to say.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: The equipment used in the failed experiment remains in her brain. No one knows for sure what will become of her.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: What? How could that be?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: It's a sad story.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Moore was an outstanding researcher who volunteered to be our test subject. You've seen what the failure of the experiment did to her.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Some measure of sacrifice is inevitable in science, but perhaps we paid too high a price.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Never mind that for now.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: I heard you went around to all the teams. Have you decided where you want to go?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I want to...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I want to use my time to help Ms. Moore.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: You want to take over her treatment?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: I thought you were interested in the research that Team 7 is conducting.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I was... but I saw how the two researchers responsible for taking care of Ms. Moore treated her.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: If she paid an inevitable price for science, I don't think she should be treated like that.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I want to help her.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I'm sure, if the same thing happened to me, you would do what you could to help me, wouldn't you?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: But it's a good idea to be prepared. Working at Rhine Lab has its risks.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Take yesterday, for example. I lost a bet and almost had to go on a vegan diet for a week. If that's not fatal, I don't know what is.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...Hehe.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: You made your choice. Now you should make your preparations.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Hopefully, you'll learn a thing or two in the process.

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: They let some fresh grad take my job?!

steps.name: Researcher D
steps.text: I thought you couldn't wait to hand it over? Now you got your wish.

steps.name: Researcher D
steps.text: (Whisper) How much time are you planning to waste on a woman who got her brain fried in an experiment?

steps.name: Researcher D
steps.text: Well, then, Ms. Moore is your responsibility now, Silence.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Wait, you haven't told me what's going on with her yet...

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: Read her medical record yourself.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Huh? Ms. Moore? Why are you standing?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Let's see here...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: 'Joyce Moore exhibits cognitive and linguistic impairments. She has difficulty communicating. Frequently talks to herself, but what she says is unintelligible...'

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You're still weak, Ms. Moore. You should go back to bed.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Is she mute?

steps.name: Joyce Moore
steps.text: Negative.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: (Come to think of it, I think she said the word 'affirmative' when we first met.)

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: (But it's impossible to tell what she's trying to convey with that word alone.)

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You're Liberi, right?

steps.name: Joyce Moore
steps.text: Affirmative.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: When you say 'affirmative', do you mean 'yes'?

steps.name: Joyce Moore
steps.text: Affirmative.

steps.name: Joyce Moore
steps.text: Warning: Potential misunderstanding.

steps.name: Joyce Moore
steps.text: Dialogue is logically valid even if 'affirmative' denotes negation of statement.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Er... let me think...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You're right!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: If 'affirmative' means 'no', you would still have answered 'affirmative' when asked whether 'affirmative' meant 'yes'.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You figured that out so quickly? Doesn't sound like cognitive impairment to me.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Anyway, it's getting late. I'll fetch you lunch from the cafeteria.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: (She's gone silent again.)

steps.name: Joyce Moore
steps.text: Warning... system... unknown error...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Ms. Moore? Ms. Joyce Moore?!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Her breathing is steady, as are her vital signs... did she just fall asleep suddenly?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: There are some similarities with my own symptoms.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: How are you feeling today, Joyce?

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Increase in flexibility detected. High intensity rehabilitation exercises possible.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Great.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But you just exercised yesterday, and it's the weekend. You should take a day off.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Dr. Silence's instructions have proven effective, indicating considerable medical expertise.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: No, I only just graduated.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Correction. Dr. Silence is a recent graduate with considerable medical expertise.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: (Blushes)

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: By the way, if you're not doing rehab today, I want to...

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: (Tilts head)

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I want to watch a show in your room.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Today not a work day. It is recommended that Dr. Silence view the show at home with friends.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Well, I don't have any frien—

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Dr. Silence is welcome to watch here, if the recommended scenario cannot be achieved.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Really?

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Affirmative.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: What is the name of the series?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Blood and Dividends.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Popcorn is recommended.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Is there popcorn in the office?

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Leave this room, turn left. Proceed one hundred and fifty meters, then turn right and proceed two hundred and seventy meters to find a popcorn vending machine on the corner. Note that caramel-flavored popcorn is suboptimal for this series.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Oh, we're out of popcorn.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: (Yawns)

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Let's take a break, Joyce.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: (Steady breathing)

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Is she asleep?

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: ...Affirmative.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: It's fine. I have an Oripathy-related sleep disorder myself, so I understand.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Dr. Silence demonstrated below-average attention during playback.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Oh, you noticed.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I'm not a huge fan of finance-themed dramas, but my colleagues are all talking about it, so I felt like I had to watch it.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Inquiry: why do you feel the need to watch the same drama?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: To fit in, I guess. Otherwise, we just don't have anything to talk about.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I'm from a backwater with very little entertainment. When I went to college, my classmates helped me a lot, and I never had to try to fit in with the crowd.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But now...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: *sigh*.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Why do you find it necessary to conform to the collective?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Dr. Silence does not appear particularly eager to build social relationships.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I... I just felt that I should establish a good relationship with my colleagues, so I could be happier at work...

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Balance must be achieved between insufficient conformity, and excessive conformity.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You're... right.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Maybe I should return this—

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: What are you doing? You watched a show with her?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You're...

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: Don't mind me, just came to get something I left.

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: Kids these days have the weirdest ideas, using a soap opera to teach her how to talk like a normal person...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: That's not it!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: And Joyce doesn't suffer from any cognitive impairment. Your reports are wrong—

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: And...?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: What do you mean by 'and'?

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: So she has normal cognitive ability. So what? What are you gonna do about it?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: What in the—how could you falsify medical records like that, reporting symptoms that don't exist?!

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: Enough, little girl. Spare me your worthless sympathy. I know her much better than you do.

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: Why do you think she's been living in the wards? It's not because of her condition. It's Device #9!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: What's the difference? Isn't Device #9 the cause of her condition?

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: Whatever... it's not like you'll listen.

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: But you'd better realize that you're the one causing trouble here. Do you know how much data your sympathy has cost us?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Data? What data are you talking about?

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: You really don't know? It's so obvious that—

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Please be quiet.

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Please be quiet.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Please be quiet, Mr. Hancock.

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: Oh, I get it now. How kind of you to try to shield this naive little girl from—

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Please. Be. Quiet.
Joyce's expression has hardly changed, but Silence can feel her anger from the way she is pausing between words.

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: ...Hmph.

steps.name: Researcher C
steps.text: Suit yourself.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: What was he trying to say? What data?

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Noise.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Noise?

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Harmful noise.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...I still don't understand.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: You will, with time.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Alright...

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Now playing Blood and Dividends, episode 7.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: That's all for this week's agenda.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Before you go, a word with you, Silence.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Of course, Dr. Parvis.

steps.name: Researcher D
steps.text: (Whisper) She screwed up, didn't she?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Silence, we need to talk about your work arrangement.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: I told you to prepare to hand over the care of Joyce Moore. How are things going on that front?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I've rectified her medical record and included a list of terms in the appendices.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: List of terms?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: As I previously reported, Joyce's linguistic capabilities are functioning perfectly well. Her condition doesn't manifest in such skin-deep ways.

steps.name: Researcher D
steps.text: (Whisper) Like hell.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Her unique speech pattern is a defense mechanism for mitigating the impact of Oripathy and the experiment. There is ample radiological and pathological evidence to support this assertion.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I have compiled a list of terms used by Joyce and their natural language equivalents, in order to make things easier for my successor.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Good work.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: However, I would prefer not to hand Joyce over to someone else.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: From a treatment perspective alone, I have no objection to the change.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: However, it takes time to change assignments, and energy to establish effective communication with Joyce. I am concerned that my successor may neglect Joyce's emotional needs. Such as...

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Such as?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...Never mind.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: (Shrugs)

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: I've heard Moore's thoughts on the matter.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: She communicated more or less the same, in her own way, requesting that you continue to be responsible for her treatment.

steps.name: Researcher D
steps.text: (Whisper) Birds of a feather.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Objectively, Moore's recovery has progressed rapidly since you took over her treatment.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: A colleague will soon return to our service, thanks to you, Silence.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I appreciate the kind words.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: However, we still have a small problem.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Team 7 has been shorthanded lately, and I would very much like to reassign you there.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: If you're not willing to give up Moore, you'll have to balance both jobs at the same time.

steps.name: Researcher D
steps.text: Her? Team 7? Two jobs at the same time?!

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: What was that, Karen?

steps.name: Researcher D
steps.text: Er, no, nothing...

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: But then I gave it some thought. Now that Moore's condition has stabilized, you should be able to devote most of your efforts to Team 7.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: I've already talked to the team lead, and we're just waiting to hear your thoughts.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: You'll have a heavy workload, balancing both Moore's treatment and the research of Team 7. Are you up to it?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Yes! It would be an honor to work on Team 7!

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: We'll be counting on you on both sides, then.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Thank you!

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Dismissed.

steps.name: Researcher A
steps.text: Wow, Olivia! That's amazing!

steps.name: Researcher B
steps.text: Don't pat her so hard, Chris.

steps.name: Researcher A
steps.text: Hehe, my bad.

steps.name: Researcher A
steps.text: OliviaLet's hit the bar tonight, Olivia. Your drinks are on me.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Thank you, Mr. Miller—no, Chris, Susanna.

steps.name: Researcher A
steps.text: No need to thank us. We want to hang out with you too. We can talk about anything!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Like... Blood and Dividends?

steps.name: Researcher A
steps.text: Of course!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I'm not so used to crowded places. Is that okay?

steps.name: Researcher B
steps.text: Of course. This is Trimounts, after all!

steps.name: Researcher B
steps.text: Who cares if you're a bit quiet in the bars, as long as you shine brightly in the labs!

steps.name: Researcher B
steps.text: As for this guy here, I'll throttle him if he asks any awkward questions.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I just can't get used to bars. Plus, I'm not much of a drinker.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Oripathy patients are advised to refrain from consuming alcohol.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I thought I asked for something non-alcoholic, but then I realized I had an alcoholic drink, and a pretty stiff one at that.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But I couldn't really refuse under the circumstances, so I took a few sips.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: The next time we go out together, I'm insisting that we go see the fountain in Trimounts Common.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Do you like the fountain in Trimounts Common?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Yes, it reminds me of a little park back home. There was an identical fountain there, just a little smaller.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: The fountain of Trimounts Common is known for its exotic design. It is possible that both fountains were built by Trimounts' Munson Inc.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Ha. I thought it was a fun coincidence, but I guess it's just Munson Inc. expanding its business into rural areas.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Dr. Silence appears to be experiencing nostalgia.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: The first few days here were tough, but I feel much better now that I have you to talk to.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Please continue to describe your hometown.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Let me think...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: It's hard to know what to say, when you ask like that.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I understand what you mean, but it's hard to find the words to describe it.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Suggestion: Departing now for Trimounts Common will be of assistance in describing your hometown.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Do you mean... you want to come with me to Trimounts Common?

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Affirmative.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: So if I say yes... this will be the first time you've left Rhine Lab HQ since the accident.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: As far as I can tell, you're fully recovered, but Dr. Parvis recommended another week of rest for you, just in case.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: There is no need to worry.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: Reason: Dr. Silence is a friend.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: The risk to health is extremely low, negligible when compared to a friend.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Thank you, Joyce!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But let's wait until next week.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: (Tilts head)

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Me being your friend is all the more reason not to ask you to take risks.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Let's go to Trimounts Common once you're fully recovered.

steps.name: Silence
